conclusions: Two healthy startup-seeded warm UI round trips preserved source; third export failed. A complete browser restart restored successful export and restore on the same source/account.
Export-only diagnostics reproduced failure on the third attempt in two separately restarted browser runs, so intervening restore activity is not necessary.

Passive CDP breakpoints on original served bytes identified not_observed during hydrate metadata, before capture. The reader/root reached failed; this was not an unknown state or download-policy rejection.
Four groups of ordinary read-only queries passed in both a Node memory client and the deployed browser persistent client. This does not isolate every difference from capture.

Page heap stayed approximately 23-28 MiB after successful UI rounds; SharedWorker target counts alone do not establish active client leaks. SDK worker closure intentionally avoids workerGlobal.close() on lease release.
The fresh-account control failed in test setup with NotObserved before backup measurement; it is not a passing fresh-account comparison.
Original exit 137 remains unattributed. No timeout increases, retries, SDK private API workaround or consistency downgrade were applied.

Fourteen-query public native capture reproduced not_observed on the third capture after two accepted zero-write commits. Sequential transaction reads also failed on the third capture; serializing reads is not a demonstrated fix.

Eight captures of the three-row accounts query passed. Four captures of the 521-row transactions query also passed, but native reads took 12.3-13.0 seconds versus 1.2-1.5 seconds for warm ordinary reads. The successful native commit waits took 0.65-0.83 seconds. These controls do not prove an ordinal third-transaction rule or identify the exact SDK/core fault.

Do not rewrite Finance orchestration to address this evidence. Investigate the public native read/coverage path with the failing multi-query reproducer while preserving remote hydration, exclusive validation and finite cleanup.

Node public SDK capture also reproduced the problem after the Finance browser was closed: two zero-write captures accepted; the next ordinary hydration queries all failed with not_observed. The harness then attempted a capture that also failed; that extra failure is not evidence of a separately valid hydrated capture. This excludes Finance UI/backup runtime as a necessary condition, but not its schema/policy or the cloud service.

A longer ordinary-read-only Node control passed 112 queries in eight groups after the Finance browser closed. That query count alone does not reproduce the native-capture failure. Exact elapsed-time, client/core, cloud service and permission-evaluation causes remain unresolved.
limits: One desktop Chromium host, one preview/backend app, synthetic 521-transaction graph; phone, maximum aggregate and storage pressure unqualified.
Passive debugger controls are diagnostic, not production latency benchmarks.
The original invalid-fixture download control also stopped on a global initialization alert; it does not establish automatic-download blocking.
A subsequent manual profile/marker setup stalled before measurement and was terminated; no passing evidence is claimed.
All native controls retain the same Finance schema/policy and cloud service. No exact client/core/server/policy defect or universally failing transaction ordinal has been isolated.

limits: One measurement per growth level in fixed order on one cloud backend/host; temporal variation is not fully excluded.

Added rows also add commit history, so live-row and history costs are not separated.
Fingerprint covers the 14 source metadata projections including audit. Workspace/profile/membership records are not in that fingerprint; the clone procedure never modifies their original IDs.
No attachments, phone, maximum aggregate or storage-pressure qualification. This is an SDK control, not full UI latency.

conclusions: A universal third-capture failure, simple 90-second connection expiry and a projection-only bug are not established. Ordinary cold reads can also fail before native capture.
Source capture latency increases with unrelated owned workspace data/history while source contents and its audit projection remain unchanged, even with a fresh SDK client at every measurement.
A browser memory leak is unnecessary to reproduce this scaling effect. Original local exit 137 remains unattributed.
The role-predicate simplification is rejected; no new Finance workaround, retry, timeout increase, consistency downgrade or SDK private API application dependency is introduced.

Investigate scoped frozen-query input/permission evaluation on the alpha.59 runtime; do not read current SQLite source as if it were the installed native core. Exact causal SDK/core/server correction remains unimplemented.
The four-workspace cloud repeat accepted once at 9.9 s and then failed in its transaction snapshot query with not_observed despite successful source hydration; preserve both outcomes.

The growth effect also occurs on the pinned local disposable memory backend: unchanged source capture took 1.219/1.998/3.683 s for one/two/four owned workspaces, with fresh SDK clients. Cloud timing alone is unnecessary.

A new owner with one workspace on that local backend, alongside four other-owner workspaces, took 3.622-3.884 s across three diagnostic captures. Backend profiling points to maintained-query graph rehydration/compilation and operator hashing.

No SDK/source patch is retained. A correction must be tested against the actual alpha.59 runtime and preserve native snapshot/predicate validation; broad Finance state-machine changes and the rejected role rewrite are unsupported by these experiments.
